what_its_for: Alitretinoin is used to treat two main conditions. The gel form (Panretin) is applied to skin sores caused by Kaposi's sarcoma, a type of cancer that can affect people with HIV/AIDS. The capsule form (Toctino) is used to treat severe chronic hand eczema (a stubborn skin condition causing red, itchy, cracked skin on the hands) that has not improved with other treatments.
how_to_take: Gel (Panretin): Apply a generous amount of gel directly onto each skin sore using your fingertip or a cotton swab. Do not rub it onto surrounding healthy skin. Let it dry before covering with clothing. Wash your hands after applying. Capsules (Toctino): Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Take it with a meal that contains some fat (such as milk or food with butter or oil) to help your body absorb the medicine better. Do not chew, crush, or open the capsule.
dosing: Gel (Panretin): Apply the gel to affected skin sores two times a day to start. Your doctor may slowly increase this to three or four times a day depending on how well you tolerate it. Capsules (Toctino): The usual starting dose is 30 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase this to 60 mg once daily based on your response and side effects. Always follow the exact dose your doctor has prescribed.
missed_dose: Gel (Panretin): If you forget a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled application, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply extra gel to make up for a missed application. Capsules (Toctino): If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the usual time. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Gel (Panretin): Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat and open flames because the gel is flammable. Keep the tube tightly closed. Capsules (Toctino): Store at room temperature below 77°F (25°C). Keep the capsules in their original packaging to protect them from light and moisture. Keep all forms of this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Do not use insect repellents containing DEET on areas where you apply the gel. Avoid getting the gel in your eyes, nose, mouth, or on healthy skin around the sores. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds while using either form of alitretinoin, as it makes your skin more sensitive to sunlight — use sunscreen and protective clothing. Do not take vitamin A supplements or other retinoid medicines (such as isotretinoin or acitretin) while using alitretinoin, as this increases the risk of side effects. Women who could become pregnant must use highly effective contraception — alitretinoin can cause serious birth defects. Do not donate blood while taking alitretinoin capsules and for at least one month after stopping treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; severe skin irritation, blistering, swelling, or pain at the application site that becomes hard to manage; symptoms of high triglycerides (fat in the blood) such as severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; signs of depression, mood changes, or unusual thoughts; severe headache, vision changes, or nausea that could be signs of high pressure in the brain; joint or bone pain; or if you think you or your partner might be pregnant.
when_it_works: Gel (Panretin): You may start to see improvement in your Kaposi's sarcoma skin sores after about 2 to 4 weeks of regular use, but it may take up to 14 to 16 weeks to see the full benefit. Do not stop using it early even if improvement seems slow. Capsules (Toctino): Most people begin to notice improvement in their hand eczema within the first 12 weeks of treatment. The full course of treatment usually lasts 12 to 24 weeks. Some people may need a longer course depending on their response.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Alitretinoin must NOT be used during pregnancy in any form. It causes severe birth defects. Women who could become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting the capsules, must use at least one — and ideally two — highly effective methods of contraception during treatment and for one month after stopping, and must have regular pregnancy tests during treatment. Men taking alitretinoin should also use condoms during treatment and for one month afterward if their partner could become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while using alitretinoin capsules, as the medicine may pass into breast milk and harm the baby. Children: Toctino capsules are not approved for use in children under 18 years of age. Panretin gel use in children should be discussed with a doctor. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor if you have any liver or kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
